words.m: existing or happening below the ground
the physical features of a piece of land
relating to the earth or to land
from beyond the earth

why: territory: Latin territorium's link to terra is disputed (Etymonline/de Vaan note a possible terrere 'frighten' origin); replaced with an unambiguous terra word

words.m: a vehicle with two wheels
able to speak two languages
involving two sides or two parties
to cut into two parts

why: binocular comes from Latin bini 'two by two', not the prefix bi- itself (Etymonline); replaced with a clean bi- word

words.m: the branch of medicine caring for children
a doctor for children
the method and practice of teaching
bone and muscle medicine; the name first meant straightening children's bodies

why: pedodontist is rare, not a common word; orthopedics (Andry's orthopédie, Greek paid- 'child') is common and genuinely contains this element

words.m: full of danger
having fame; well known
full of joy
full of courage; brave

why: nervous (Latin nervosus 'sinewy') does not show the 'full of' meaning in its modern sense; courageous does

words.m: a wide view of an entire area
a disease outbreak that spreads across many countries or the whole world
a cure for all problems
telling a story with gestures only

why: a pandemic is spread over a wide area such as multiple countries, not just one country

words.m: a gas named from the Greek for 'new'
relating to newborn babies
in a later style that revives ancient Greek and Roman art
a beginner; a newcomer

why: neoclassical is an adjective; gloss reworded to match and be precise

set.note: Spelling changes with the next letter: com- before b, m, p; col- before l (collect); cor- before r (correct); co- usually before vowels and h; con- before most others.

why: note omitted the col-/cor- forms, so 'con- before most others' misleads for l and r
intra- 'within, inside' overlaps with in- 'in, into'
in- 'in, into' overlaps with intra- 'within, inside'
-ous 'having the quality of' overlaps with -ish 'having the qualities of'
bene- and eu- both show the identical choice 'good, well' (duplicate option text)
anthrop 'human being, humankind' overlaps with dem 'people'
phon 'sound, voice' is too close to dict 'say, speak'
hypo- 'under, below' is too close to de- 'down'
